unit.why: A footnote, quoted from the end of Be'erot ha-Mayim, tells how the Maggid of Kozienice challenged God during Kol Nidre in his last year until He said 'salachti', followed by the Rizhiner's and the Seer of Lublin's reactions.
unit.boundary_note: A page break drops in an unrelated footnote fragment: a saying on gilgul from Imrei Elimelekh ('בינו שנות דור ודור'), ending at 'יותר מגיהנם *). (אמרי אלימלך ויחי)'. The story then resumes at 'ויתרון מפאת'. That gilgul passage belongs to another note, which continues in the next division.

stories.start_quote: אמרתי להביא פה מעשה מרבינו המגיד מקאזניץ
stories.end_quote: החולה השוכב על מטתו הרעיש כל העולמות
stories.summary_en: In his last year, the frail Maggid of Kozienice argued with God at Kol Nidre before 'Vayomer Hashem salachti': he named the tzaddikim of the generation and offered to repent for all Israel himself. Then he had the singers sing and cried out 'salachti'. Hearing the story, the Rizhiner said the Maggid had heard 'salachti' from God's own mouth, and the Seer of Lublin had sensed the event that same night.
